verdict.summary: The PR introduces a fallback mechanism that embeds AI-generated findings directly into Markdown without sanitization, creating a potential injection vector if an attacker can influence the model's output (e.g., via prompt injection). No authentication, secrets, or supply-chain issues are introduced.
verdict.confidenceReason: The injection risk is real but depends on GitHub's Markdown sanitization and the attacker's ability to influence the model; no other security concerns are present.

findings.headline: Unsanitized AI-generated content embedded in Markdown body enables potential injection
findings.body: `buildFallbackBody` and `renderFindingsByFile` concatenate `f.headline`, `f.body`, and `f.path` directly into a Markdown string without any escaping or sanitization. If an attacker can influence the AI model's output (e.g., via prompt injection in PR description or code comments), they could inject malicious Markdown or HTML (e.g., `<script>`, `javascript:` links). While GitHub's Markdown renderer typically sanitizes, bypasses exist and the risk is non-zero. Mitigate by sanitizing all user-controlled fields (headline, body, path) before embedding them in the body, e.g., using a Markdown escape library or stripping HTML tags.

verdict.summary: No performance regressions found. The fallback path is a cold path (only fires on submit errors), pure helpers are O(n log n) at worst, and the single immediate retry adds at most one extra GitHub API call per failed submission — no retry loop, no unbounded growth, no hot-path allocation churn.
verdict.confidenceReason: All changed code is either pure rendering functions called once per review or a single sequential retry on a cold error path; nothing touches hot paths, loops, or concurrent state.

feat(phase4a): submit-review fallback when inline anchors are rejected

## Summary

GitHub validates every inline-anchor in a `POST /reviews` and rejects the entire submission on a single bad position (typical 422). Phase 4a's orchestrator caught this as `internal_error` and silently fell back to Phase 3 — losing a good ensemble verdict because of one bad line number.

This PR ports Greptile's pr_review.ts pattern: catch the submit error, retry the same review WITHOUT inline comments, embedding every finding in the body as markdown grouped by file.

## Changes

- **`buildFallbackSubmission`** + **`buildFallbackBody`** (pure, exported) in `src/lib/triage-pr-review.ts`. Renders findings grouped by file, sorted by score DESC then line ASC. Preserves the `<!-- openclaw:pr-review -->` dedupe marker so existing dedupe-by-marker logic still recognizes the comment.
- **`validateForSubmission()`** now returns `unanchoredFindings` — findings that passed the hallucination guard but failed `deriveSide()` (line not in diff). The fallback recovers these (no inline anchoring → position-validity stops mattering); the inline path drops them as before.
- **Orchestrator wraps `submitReview`** in inner try/catch. On any submit error, retries via `buildFallbackSubmission` and records `submitFallback: true` + `submitFallbackReason: <error>` in telemetry. If the fallback ALSO fails, the outer try/catch records `internal_error` — same behaviour as before this PR.

## Tests

- 20 new in `tests/submit-review-fallback.test.ts` covering `buildFallbackBody` (10), `buildFallbackSubmission` (5), and the `unanchoredFindings` field on `validateForSubmission` (4).
- All 470 existing tests still pass.
- Typecheck clean.

## Source

Pattern ported from [github.com/greptileai/examples/pr-review-bot/src/apps/pr_review.ts](https://github.com/greptileai/examples/tree/main/pr-review-bot).

## Test plan

- [x] All existing tests pass on the branch
- [x] New unit tests for `buildFallbackBody` cover marker preservation, file grouping, score-sort within file, anchored+unanchored merge, multi-line range rendering, empty-findings degenerate case
- [x] New unit tests for `buildFallbackSubmission` cover no-comments-array invariant, event preservation, commit_id pass-through
- [x] New unit tests for `validateForSubmission` cover unanchoredFindings population (line-invalid → in; hallucinated → out; score-1 → out)
- [ ] Once merged + deployed to shadow mode, watch telemetry for `submitFallback: true` events to confirm path fires when expected

Closes ARC-154.
